## Purpose

Git tracks the analysis logic: README notes, scripts, metadata tables, configuration, logs, and small final result tables. GitHub provides remote backup, collaboration, and submission infrastructure.

## What to version

- README and workflow notes.
- Sample metadata and accession tables.
- Scripts and command notes under `scripts/`.
- Configuration files.
- Small summary tables and final figures.

## What not to version

- FASTQ, BAM, BAI, CRAM, SRA, bigWig, large archives, temporary files, and tool caches.
- Passwords, tokens, unpublished private data, or confidential student information.

## Minimal commands

```bash
git init
git status
git add README.md .gitignore raw_data/metadata reference_genome scripts results/logs
git commit -m "Initialize reproducible NGS project"
git remote add origin git@github.com:USERNAME/PROJECT.git
git push -u origin main
```

## Commit checkpoints

Use small commits after meaningful stages: structure, metadata, retrieval plan, reference, RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, integration, and final slides.
